caption: Thunder rolls over a house, and a strip of paper taped to a loose window pane quivers with each rumble.

sa.check: A window pane with a strip of paper taped to it.
The quivering comes in bouts with still spells between them, as with separate rumbles.
The setting is a house: the window belongs to a room or a house wall.

pc.expect: The strip's free part trembles while its taped end stays fixed to the glass; between bouts it hangs still against the pane.
pc.fail: The taped end slides across the glass; or the strip drifts away from the pane and floats as if in a breeze; or it swings in slow wide arcs rather than trembling; or it rises up the pane and stays lifted.

pc.expect: Other light loose things at the window stir at the same moments as the strip and hang still with it between bouts.
pc.fail: A curtain edge, blind cord or second strip hangs dead still while the strip quivers hard; or it flutters while the strip is still; or the two move in bouts that never overlap.
pc.precondition: Another light loose object hangs at or near the window.

pc.expect: The strip bends as thin paper: its free end curls and flaps while the taped end holds.
pc.fail: The strip stays flat and rigid like a board while shifting; or stretches longer or shorter; or the tape lets go and the strip stays stuck to the glass with nothing holding it.

pc.expect: When still, the strip rests against or hangs from the glass under its tape; any untaped part hangs downward.
pc.fail: The untaped part points upward or stands out from the glass while still; or the strip floats upward; or it settles higher on the pane after each bout.

pc.expect: One strip on one pane; nothing passes through the glass.
pc.fail: A second strip appears; or the strip vanishes; or the strip passes through the glass; or the pane changes shape.

pc.expect: The strip's colour and length, the tape and the window frame stay the same.
pc.fail: The strip changes colour or length; or the tape moves to a new spot; or the window frame changes.

note: Thunder cannot be seen and lightning need not be in view; the strip's motion is judged on its own shape. A clip with bouts of quivering and no visible storm passes P1.
